mission_06: Local Outlier Factor (LOF) is a density-based anomaly detection method that identifies outliers based on the local density deviation of a point compared to its neighbors. Unlike global methods that use a single threshold for the entire dataset, LOF computes a local density for each point and compares it to the densities of its neighbors. Points with significantly lower local density than their neighbors receive high LOF scores and are flagged as outliers. This makes LOF particularly effective for datasets with varying density regions, where a point may be an outlier in a dense cluster but appear normal in a sparse region. The n_neighbors parameter controls the locality of the density estimation, with smaller values detecting more local anomalies and larger values capturing more global patterns.
